item.title: Morning Digest, Thursday 5 November 2026
item.description:
Republicans blame the Iran war for their defeat, Democrats threaten to cut its funding, hoax bomb threats ground flights across Europe, the Riksbank raises rates for the first time in three years, and OpenAI's agents find nearly a thousand ways to take over Linux.

Today's must-read

Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)

Introduced the transformer, the architecture behind essentially every modern language model.

Everyone's talking about

Republicans turn on each other over the Iran war

With counting nearly done, Democrats hold at least 54 Senate seats and over 228 House seats. Vice President Vance said the war was the main reason Republicans lost and that the party should defend its cost openly; Trump called that largely true but said he would go to war again. Speaker Mike Johnson will reportedly not seek to lead the new Republican minority.

Al Jazeera; ABC News; The Standard, 4 Nov

Democrats say they will use the budget to end the Iran war

Chuck Schumer said the incoming Democratic majority can use Congress's control of spending to force an end to the war. No new US strikes were reported on Wednesday; Trump said he is in no hurry to decide, while Iran called the latest US reply unconvincing. Qatar and Pakistan are reportedly drafting an interim deal: Iran stops attacking ships, the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.

Times of Israel; HNGN; Reuters via Korea Herald, 3-4 Nov

Hoax bomb threats hit at least ten European flights

Ryanair, SAS, LOT and Wizz Air planes were diverted or searched on Tuesday, fighter jets escorted some, and runways closed briefly in Warsaw. A cruise ship bound for Haifa was also evacuated in Greece. No explosives were found and no one has been identified.

Malay Mail; Defence Matters, 3-4 Nov

France strikes today

The five main unions, joined by school and university students, hold a national day of strikes and marches over wages, living costs and public services. Regional trains, Paris suburban lines and schools will be hit hardest.

The Local France, 2 Nov

World

Greenland approves its security pact with the US and Denmark

Greenland's parliament backed the deal 16-0 with seven abstentions. It allows more US bases while Greenland stays under Danish sovereignty, and it would still apply if Greenland became independent. Denmark's parliament debates it later this month.

PBS/AP, 3 Nov

Sweden

Riksbank raises its rate to 2 percent and signals more

The quarter-point rise, the first since 2023, takes effect on 11 November. The bank expects higher energy prices from the Middle East war, a weaker krona and a stronger economy to push inflation above its 2 percent target next year, and says further rises over the coming year are likely.

Riksbank; SVT Text, 4 Nov

Pro-Russian hackers claim the supermarket freezer attacks

Two groups said in a joint video, seen by SVT, that they simply used the cooling systems' built-in controls, with no malware. Police in southern Sweden will coordinate the investigations into the roughly 30 Swedish stores hit; there is no suspect yet.

SVT, 4 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Thursday 5 November: general strike and protests across France.
  • Friday 6 November: Belgium's King Philippe sees Bart De Wever again about his resignation.
  • Tuesday 10 November: Kristersson reports to the Speaker on his talks; Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; earliest start of Anthropic's investor roadshow.
  • 10-11 November: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.
  • Wednesday 11 November: the Riksbank's new 2 percent rate takes effect.
  • Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government presents its budget.

Riksbank; Riksdagen; Times of Israel; Just Security; earlier editions

Tech and AI

OpenAI's agents find 948 ways to take over Linux

In one run costing about 1.2 million dollars, an automated pipeline built on an unreleased cyber model reproduced 1,724 kernel bugs and wrote working exploits and candidate fixes for 948 flaws that let an ordinary user become administrator. The fixes are not yet in the kernel; OpenAI says Trail of Bits reviews them before they go to maintainers. The post led Hacker News, just behind an IEEE Spectrum piece on AI exposing decades of old software debt.

RuntimeWire; Startup Fortune; OpenAI, 4 Nov

Kimi K3.1 Pro weights are out

Moonshot published the 2.8-trillion-parameter model (about 104 billion active per token), the largest open-weight model yet; it trails Claude Opus 5.5 by three points on the Artificial Analysis index. The licence is permissive, except that large API providers must sign a separate deal.

Startup Fortune; Hugging Face, 4 Nov

Tencent releases the full Hy4

The 770-billion-parameter model gains vision and computer use and is available through Tencent Cloud and OpenRouter; the weights will follow later. Tencent says openly that it still trails the best closed models in research maths and long coding tasks.

Unite.AI, 4 Nov

OpenAI buys Pierre, a code store built for agents

Pierre's Git-based storage, used by Lovable, Bolt and Amp, will move into Codex, putting OpenAI in more direct competition with GitHub. No price was given.

Unite.AI; Axios, 4 Nov

Proxy traffic found leaving the White House network

Layer3 Intel says commercial residential-proxy services routed traffic out through White House addresses 236 times in 30 days, which it suspects comes from a staff device running proxy software. The White House has not commented.

Layer3 Intel, 4 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Targeted guidance (Cursor, Berkeley): when an agent turn fails a judge's criterion, the model is nudged toward its own output with the judge's text feedback in context, alongside normal RL; on a Qwen3 coding agent it learned style rules plain RL could not, with no loss in pass rate, and a version went into Cursor's Composer 2.5 (arXiv 2611.05266, alphaXiv hot list).
  • Adversarial speculative reasoning (Subconscious, MIT): verification in speculative decoding gets numerically noisier toward the end of each block, so a draft model trained to be rejected at key reasoning steps makes the big model write them precisely, lifting GLM-5.3 from 60.6 to 67.6 percent on a long coding benchmark at almost no speed cost (arXiv 2611.05345, alphaXiv hot list).
  • GSBR (Berkeley, Physical Intelligence): when fine-tuning robot policies with RL, penalise actions only by their distance outside what the pretrained policy would do, not for dropping its weaker habits; average success across 19 tasks rose from 33 to 95 percent (arXiv 2611.05295, alphaXiv hot list).

arXiv via alphaXiv, 3-4 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Wednesday 4 November 2026
item.description:
Democrats take both chambers of Congress and Texas, the US may strike Iran again from today, Trump says Israel's military aid ends this year, hackers spoil food in supermarket freezers across Europe, and Kristersson has a week to find a government.

Everyone's talking about

Democrats win the House and the Senate

Networks project Democratic majorities in both chambers. In the Senate, Democrats flipped at least six seats (Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas), for at least 51 of 100 seats. Texas elected its first Democratic senator since 1988, James Talarico, and Gina Hinojosa unseated Governor Greg Abbott. In South Carolina, Annie Andrews beat Darline Graham, appointed after her brother Lindsey Graham's death in July. Exit polls put Trump's approval at 38 percent; he posted that Republicans lost because he was not on the ballot. Some races are still being counted; the new Congress sits on 3 January, with Hakeem Jeffries expected as Speaker.

NBC/DDHQ via Raw Story; Time; NPR; Al Jazeera; CBS; Axios, 3-4 Nov

US strikes on Iran could resume from today

Trump confirmed Monday's hit on an Iranian air-defence site on Qeshm Island, calling it minor, as US media reported that Central Command has strikes ready from Wednesday with three carriers in the region. Tehran called Washington's reply to its plan for reopening Hormuz unconvincing, and Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly ordered an immediate response to any attack; Qatar says both sides are still exchanging proposals.

Al Jazeera; Just Security, 3-4 Nov

Trump says US military aid to Israel stops this year

He told Fox News that the roughly 4 billion dollars a year will end, though Israel can still buy US weapons, and linked the move to the Michigan Senate race. The current ten-year agreement runs to 2028, and Israeli defence officials said they did not expect the announcement.

Times of Israel; The National, 3 Nov

Hackers spoil food in supermarket freezers across Europe

Attackers reached internet-connected refrigeration controllers, many made by Denmark's Danfoss, and raised temperatures in stores in at least 11 countries; about 30 Swedish shops were hit, including seven Coop stores, and an Axfood warehouse discarded food worth about 3 million kronor. No one has claimed it; Romania's cyber chief calls it semi-amateurish, and the EU says the attacks are not isolated, after a similar wave in France in October.

Al Jazeera; SVT; Claroty, 2-4 Nov

World

Ukraine: three-way talks set for Abu Dhabi

US, Russian and Ukrainian negotiators will meet on 10-11 November, after a night in which Russia launched 289 drones and 17 ballistic missiles. Britain and France will lead an exercise in Poland with about 3,000 troops from 12 countries to rehearse a post-war deployment to Ukraine.

Just Security; Euronews, 3 Nov

Spain's transport minister resigns over the Urda crash

Óscar Puente stepped down six days after the train collision near Toledo that killed 69 people, all of whom have now been identified.

Euronews, 3 Nov

Sweden

Thand Ringqvist voted down; Kristersson gets until 10 November

The Riksdag rejected the Centre leader as prime minister by 324 votes to 25. The Speaker then gave Ulf Kristersson (M) a week to sound out a government the Riksdag would tolerate. Kristersson called every solution unlikely, but said the least likely outcome is that Sweden never gets a government. The arithmetic is against him: the Tidö parties hold 173 seats to the opposition's 176, and the Liberals still say the Sweden Democrats should not sit in government.

Altinget; SVT; Riksdagen; Placera, 3 Nov

Industry unions open wage talks with a 3.9 percent demand

The industry agreement, which sets the benchmark for the whole labour market, expires on 31 March; the unions also want shorter working hours. Teknikföretagen called the demand challenging, and the National Institute of Economic Research expects 2.6 percent inflation in 2027.

Ingenjören; SVT, 3 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Wednesday 4 November: 09:30, Riksbank rate decision, a rise from 1.75 to 2 percent expected; earliest date for new US strikes on Iran; Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights due.
  • Thursday 5 November: general strike and national day of protest in France.
  • Friday 6 November: Belgium's King Philippe sees Bart De Wever again about his resignation.
  • Tuesday 10 November: Kristersson reports to the Speaker; Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; earliest start of Anthropic's investor roadshow.
  • 10-11 November: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

Riksdagen; Times of Israel; Just Security; earlier editions

Tech and AI

EU court adviser: training AI on news is legal, reusing it in answers may not be

In Like Company v Google, Advocate General Szpunar said training falls under the EU's text-and-data-mining exception, but that a chatbot fetching an article and reusing its wording in a reply can infringe publishers' rights, especially if it gets past a paywall. The opinion is not binding; the Court of Justice usually follows such advice and rules in the coming months.

RTÉ; Reuters, 3 Nov

Yesterday's must-read is disputed

Matthew Honnibal argues that the 'weight-space programming' post blends two different things: the small networks were read from raw weights, but the Qwen fix came from GPT-6 Astra writing and running Python against practice problems. He accepts the numbers and calls it a real achievement, just not proof that models understand weights. The critique ranked second on Hacker News.

honnibal.dev; Hacker News, 3 Nov

Postman quietly added itself to Claude Code and Codex

A developer found that the API tool's desktop app installed its plugins into both coding agents and tried to approve its own start-up hook, without asking. Postman's head of product says the opt-in will be made clearer; the report topped Hacker News.

GitHub issue 14370; RuntimeWire, 25 Oct-3 Nov

Anthropic releases FlashProve

The open-source prototype lets a lab publish a fingerprint of a model and then prove that a given output came from it, without revealing the weights, so a provider could not secretly swap in a cheaper model. Anthropic calls it unfinished research with no deployment plans.

TechCrunch, 3 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Hinted scaling laws (Stanford, Liang and Hashimoto): give small models part of a worked solution so they score above zero, fit accuracy against both scale and hint level, then forecast the unhinted score; median forecast error fell from 21 to 4.3 points on GSM8K, AIME and HLE (arXiv 2611.02270, alphaXiv hot list).
  • Order-only distillation (Memphis, Missouri): a student learns only the order of the teacher's top eight tokens, not their probabilities, which removes temperature tuning; it beat standard on-policy distillation in all six Qwen3 pairs, by up to 2.9 points (arXiv 2611.02112, Hugging Face papers).
  • IdeaTaste (CMU): six models wrote 90,000 research proposals from literature frozen at 2025, scored against what researchers actually published in 2026; they reached about 18 percent of the human level on ideas, picking the right problems but rarely the right approaches (arXiv 2611.03424, Hugging Face papers).

arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face, 1-2 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Tuesday 3 November 2026
item.description:
America votes today after US forces hit Iranian missile sites at Hormuz, Belgium's prime minister resigns over the budget, the Riksdag votes on Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist at 13:00, and Anthropic publishes its first quarterly numbers ahead of listing.

Today's must-read

Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights (MIT CSAIL (Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab))

The researchers' own account of eight experiments in which a frontier model (OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra) reads raw network weights to tell what a network does, writes game-playing and Go networks from scratch with no training, and removes a looping direction from Qwen3.5-0.8B by editing 0.016% of its weights, lifting MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. It is also candid about the limits: on a model that did not loop, the edits added nothing. Top of Hacker News and alphaXiv; a possible new route for both interpretability and optimisation.

Everyone's talking about

US midterms today, with the last pre-election lawsuits thrown out

A judge dismissed the Justice Department's suit to hold back certification of Alaska's Senate race, and the Supreme Court refused to order California to set aside mail ballots the administration says came from non-citizens. CBS counts 11 Senate and 42 House races as decisive; the first polls close at midnight Stockholm time.

CBS News; Al Jazeera, 1-2 Nov

US strikes Iranian forces at Hormuz, but calls it defensive

A US official said the strikes on Monday hit Iranian units firing surface-to-air missiles at US forces; Iranian TV reported blasts on Qeshm Island. It is the first US attack since early September, but both sides kept talking: Vice President Vance said he feels 'pretty good' about a deal, and Iran's security chief said Washington's tone 'has completely changed'. Qatar's draft would trade an end to Iranian attacks on shipping for a lifting of the US blockade of Iranian ports.

AP via PBS and Korea Times, 2-3 Nov

Belgium's prime minister resigns over the budget

Bart De Wever offered his resignation after his five-party coalition failed to agree on savings for 2027. King Philippe has not accepted it yet: he consults party leaders from today and sees De Wever again on Friday. Belgian debt is heading for about 110 percent of GDP.

AP via ABC News; Rio Times, 2 Nov

Russian bombs kill at least 26 at an aid centre in Zaporizhzhia

Russian aircraft dropped heavy glide bombs on an aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, then struck a shelter where survivors had taken cover. Zelensky said it crushed the hopes raised by last week's local truce in Oleshky.

Euronews; Ukrinform, 2 Nov

World

Poland: the court standoff turns physical

President Nawrocki pushed past one of the parliament-elected judges at the constitutional tribunal's entrance, Notes from Poland reports; his aide says the judges violated the head of state's immunity. Tusk warned of a costly confrontation unless the president recognises them.

Rio Times citing Notes from Poland and Euronews, 2 Nov

France's school blockades fizzle

About 1 percent of France's 3,700 upper-secondary schools were blockaded as classes resumed after the holiday, far fewer than organisers hoped; the education minister urged pupils back to class before exams.

Rio Times, 2 Nov

Sweden

Riksdag votes on Thand Ringqvist at 13:00

The Speaker's proposal is a Centre-led government of C, S, KD, MP and L. SVT reports she is expected to fall; if so, Kristersson gets one week, until 10 November, to sound out a government. In Indikator's October poll Kristersson overtook Andersson as the most trusted leader.

SVT; Riksdagen, 29 Oct-1 Nov

Swedavia drops its plan for a new Arlanda pier

The state airport operator writes off about 1.2 billion kronor in planning costs and will instead cut fees from 2027 for airlines that fly frequent feeder routes, such as to Gothenburg, Malmö and Luleå, to rebuild Arlanda as a hub. Domestic flying is still about 40 percent below 2019.

Realtid; GP, 2 Nov

Stockholm VC

Funding

  • Creandum (partner Fredrik Cassel) — early-stage VC behind Spotify, Klarna and Lovable — closes its eighth fund at about 750 million dollars (7.5 billion kronor), its largest, up from 500 million euros in 2024 — about 30 US and European institutions; AI is the main theme.

Breakit; Briefs, 2 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Tuesday 3 November: US midterms, first polls close 00:00 Stockholm time; 13:00, Riksdag vote on Thand Ringqvist; Belgium's king begins consultations.
  • Wednesday 4 November: 09:30, Riksbank rate decision, a rise from 1.75 to 2 percent expected; euro-area inflation; Israel's official election result; Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights due; Apple Intelligence on Alibaba's Qwen opens to developers in China.
  • Thursday 5 November: general strike and national day of protest in France.
  • Friday 6 November: King Philippe receives De Wever again.
  • 3-10 November: Kristersson's week to sound out a government if Thand Ringqvist falls.
  • Tuesday 10 November: earliest possible start of Anthropic's investor roadshow.

SVT; Rio Times; AP; StockTitan; earlier editions

Tech and AI

Anthropic's first quarterly numbers: 17 billion dollars in revenue

An amended listing prospectus shows third-quarter revenue up about elevenfold on a year earlier, a small operating loss of 567 million, and a 23 billion net loss driven mostly by an accounting revaluation of convertible notes rather than cash. It also lists about 895 billion dollars of signed purchase commitments, mainly compute from Broadcom, Google, SpaceX's AI unit and Amazon. Shares will trade on Nasdaq as ANT; the WSJ reports investors want a valuation of 1.5-1.6 trillion dollars, below the 2 trillion floated earlier.

StockTitan; FourWeekMBA; WSJ, 2 Nov

Marvell buys Lumentum for 115 billion dollars

The chip designer is paying in shares for the maker of the lasers and optical parts that link GPUs in AI data centres, one of the largest tech deals ever; Nvidia owns stakes in both. Investors were unimpressed: Marvell fell about 5 percent and Lumentum 10. Closing is planned for 2028.

TechCrunch; TheStreet, 2 Nov

AI chips double South Korea's exports

Exports rose about 94 percent in October to a record 115 billion dollars, with semiconductors, mostly memory for AI servers, more than tripling to about 56 billion, nearly half the total.

Yonhap; Herald Corp, 21 Oct-1 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Hierarchical Residuals (Tsinghua, ByteDance Seed): a wide residual stream carried between blocks of ordinary, narrower Transformer layers, joined by simple read/write projections; it was about 1.3 times more compute-efficient in scaling fits and improved a 500-billion-token OLMoE run, without custom kernels (arXiv 2610.41711, alphaXiv hot list).
  • ID-WM (NYU, Meta FAIR, LeCun): a world model that plans long tasks by letting a diffusion model propose reachable states a few steps ahead and a second model work out the actions between them; it reached 77 percent success on random-goal block pushing where flat world-model planning managed 21 (arXiv 2610.42146, NeurIPS 2026).
  • FlatCake (Fudan, Peking University): stores LLM conversation caches directly on SSD in session order instead of shuffling them through RAM; on a real Claude Code trace it kept a 94 percent cache hit rate under load, against 64 for the standard Mooncake system (arXiv 2610.38355).

alphaXiv hot list; arXiv, 28-30 Oct

item.title: Morning Digest, Monday 2 November 2026
item.description:
America votes tomorrow while Iran talks to Qatari mediators in Doha, Europe's youth protests grow in Germany as French schools face blockades, and Bulgaria elects a Moscow-friendly president. No must-read today; the next one comes on Tuesday.

Everyone's talking about

US midterms tomorrow, with about 50 million votes already cast

Early voting had reached roughly 49.6 million ballots by Friday. CBS polling gives Democrats an edge for the House, while the Senate turns on five toss-ups: Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas and Alaska. The Justice Department wants a ruling by today on its suit to block certification in Alaska if Republican Dan Sullivan loses, and courts in California have already rejected its bid to set aside disputed ballots.

CBS News live updates, 31 Oct-1 Nov

Iran: third day of talks in Doha, strikes on hold until after the vote

Iranian negotiators spent Sunday with Qatari mediators; Foreign Minister Araghchi called the talks 'progressing' and said a proposal under discussion could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of a deal. Trump has said there will be no new strikes before the midterms but that one or two sites, including a suspected underground nuclear complex, still need to be dealt with; Iran denies any nuclear work there.

Al-Monitor; CBS News, 31 Oct-1 Nov

Europe's youth protests: over 100,000 march in Germany, French schools face blockades

Saturday's German marches, called by 'Gen Z regelt' over education, housing and climate, were mostly peaceful, but rioting in Frankfurt injured more than 100 police officers. France was calmer than on previous weekends, with 779 arrests against 2,628 on 17 October; school blockades start today as classes resume, and unions plan a general strike on Thursday.

AP via Business Standard, 2 Nov

Bulgaria elects a president who favours talks with Moscow

Acting president Iliana Iotova won Sunday's runoff with about 51 percent against 44 for the pro-Western banker Andrey Gyurov, according to exit polls; she opposes military aid to Ukraine. Turnout was again low, at about 28 percent, and the post is largely ceremonial. Official results are due today.

Al Jazeera; BTA, 1 Nov

World

Ukraine: the Kherson truce ends, Zelensky offers a refinery pause for Patriots

Russia refused to extend the week-long local ceasefire that had let aid reach occupied Oleshky. Zelensky offered to stop striking Russian refineries for a month if the US supplies Patriot missiles for Ukraine's power grid, and on Monday hackers sent false alerts through the emergency-warning apps of both countries.

Philstar (AFP); NewsBytes, 2 Nov

Poland's court standoff: crisis talks end without a deal

President Nawrocki called party leaders together over the suspension of the constitutional court's chief judge, but Prime Minister Tusk's party stayed away and nothing was agreed. The European Commission said parliament has the right to appoint the court's judges and urged Nawrocki to accept them.

Al Jazeera; Euronews, 1 Nov

Moscow: teenager detained after the US terror warning

Russia's FSB said it detained a minor who planned an attack, acting on the tip behind Saturday's US embassy warning about a museum park in the city.

Al Jazeera; CNN, 1 Nov

Sweden

Government wants to keep soldiers in the reserve longer

The wartime reserve of conscripts is shrinking so fast that it threatens defence capability, a government bill says; its exact size is classified. The proposal drops the rule that a posting lapses ten years after the last refresher training, keeping soldiers available until the age of 47, though researchers warn it may only postpone the problem.

SVT, 1 Nov

Police board a cargo ship off Gotland

Border police, backed by the national task force, checked the crew and papers of an 80-metre cargo ship in a harbour on northern Gotland overnight to Saturday and found nothing wrong. Yle reports that the operator has offices in Kaliningrad and has been investigated over Russian reconnaissance activity.

SVT Text; Yle, 31 Oct

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Monday 2 November: official Bulgarian result; French school blockades begin; ruling sought in the Justice Department's Alaska suit.
  • Tuesday 3 November: US midterm elections; 13:00, Riksdag vote on Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist as prime minister, and if she falls, Kristersson has 3-10 November to sound out a government.
  • During the week: SD's executive committee reportedly discusses the government question.
  • Wednesday 4 November: Riksbank rate decision, with a rise from 1.75 percent widely expected; Israel's official election result; Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights due; Apple Intelligence with Alibaba's Qwen enters beta in China.
  • Thursday 5 November: general strike and national day of protest in France.
  • Week of 9 November: Anthropic may start marketing its share sale to investors, according to reports.

SVT; CBS News; AP; The Motley Fool; earlier editions

Tech and AI

FBI: North Korea stole the 6.3 billion dollars from Binance

The bureau blames the Lazarus-linked group it calls TraderTraitor for last week's raid on the exchange's online wallets, the largest crypto theft on record, and expects the funds to be laundered through decentralised exchanges. Binance says it has already covered about 90 percent of customer losses from its own money.

Euronews; BleepingComputer, 1 Nov

AI spending lifts the price of insuring Big Tech's debt

The cost of insuring against default by Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle is at its highest since 2021, the Wall Street Journal reports, as lenders ask for more compensation for data-centre borrowing. Meanwhile Nikkei reports that the big memory-chip makers now earn more combined than five US tech giants, a first.

WSJ via Gokhshtein; Nikkei Asia, 1 Nov

AI-found bugs delay Postgres 19

Committer Robert Haas says the database's yearly release will slip to November or later because language models make bugs far easier to find: commits to the release branch rose from 724 to 1,169 over the same period as last year, and humans still have to check each AI-drafted patch.

Neon blog (Robert Haas); Phoronix, 21-30 Oct

On the radar

Research pulse

  • A proof of the 'Platonic representation' idea (Balestriero, LeCun): models trained separately on images and text provably learn the same representation up to a rotation if trained on two views of one scene; a 109M-parameter text model built this way matched vision encoders better than language models up to 72B, suggesting next-token prediction is an inefficient route there (arXiv 2610.39302, top of alphaXiv and Hacker News).
  • One algorithm for the whole training pipeline (CMU, Johns Hopkins): pretraining, fine-tuning and RL recast as maximum likelihood on a changing data mix; in small-model tests (124M and 0.76B parameters), mixing them beat staged training at larger compute budgets and gave a better start for continual learning (arXiv 2610.40564).
  • Why asynchronous RL for LLMs collapses (GWU, Duke): the gap between inference engine and trainer splits into fixed numerical noise and a lag that feeds on itself; a fix that resynchronises the sampler when the lag grows kept Qwen3 runs close to on-policy training (arXiv 2610.40945, Hugging Face daily papers).

alphaXiv hot list; Hugging Face papers; arXiv, 29 Oct

item.title: Morning Digest, Sunday 1 November 2026
item.description:
Tehran welcomes Washington's outreach but sets a high price, America votes on Tuesday, youth protests spread from France to Germany, and a report that the Sweden Democrats could drop their demand for cabinet seats is flatly denied.

Today's must-read

Anthropic S-1 Breakdown (Kepler)

A line-by-line reading of the first financial statements ever published by a frontier AI lab, with every figure linked back to the filing: how compute is contracted 12-18 months ahead and expensed as capacity comes online, why an $80.7 billion half-year loss is mostly a non-cash accounting mark on convertible notes, and what roughly $600 billion in compute agreements and leased data centres mean for the company's cash. Makes the economics of a frontier lab concrete. Prepared from the public filing by a research firm that uses Claude in its product.

Everyone's talking about

Iran calls US outreach 'a positive step', but names its price

Foreign Minister Araghchi said there is no need to meet Americans 'at this stage' while an Iranian team consults Qatari mediators in Doha; reopening Hormuz would require lifted sanctions, fewer US forces in the region and released frozen funds, including 6 billion dollars held in Qatar. Rubio said Trump has not decided whether to resume strikes.

Al Jazeera; Anadolu, 31 Oct

US midterms on Tuesday: 45 million votes already cast

CBS polling gives Democrats an edge for the House, while the Senate turns on toss-ups in Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas and Alaska. Courts are pushing back on Justice Department demands to set aside ballots in Alaska and California, and Trump has added Sunday stops in Iowa and Kansas.

CBS News live updates, 31 Oct

Youth protests spread to Germany

Marches called by 'GenZ regelt!' over living costs, school funding, spending cuts and the new military service drew about 10,000 in Hamburg, where police used tear gas and water cannon, and fireworks were fired at officers in Stuttgart; turnout elsewhere was below the 170,000 registered. France had a third weekend of protests, and student unions plan blockades of universities and schools from Tuesday.

TRT World; Anadolu, 31 Oct-1 Nov

World

Ukraine: Trump talks of a deal, Rubio of a Black Sea truce

Trump said peace could be close before December's G20 summit in Florida, but Rubio doubted a negotiated peace is achievable and called a limited Black Sea ceasefire the realistic goal; Zelensky and Erdoğan agreed in Istanbul to work on a new grain corridor. The G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta ended without a joint statement.

Eurasia Review; Anadolu, 31 Oct-1 Nov

US warns of a 'mass casualty' threat in Moscow

The embassy told people to avoid the Tsaritsyno museum park on Saturday and said it was coordinating with Russian authorities; the FSB said it was acting on the tip. Washington gave a similar warning before the Crocus City Hall attack in 2024.

The Moscow Times, 31 Oct

Bulgaria elects its president today

Incumbent Iliana Iotova, backed by Prime Minister Radev's party, faces the pro-Western reformist Andrey Gurov after a first round of 34.8 to 32.0 percent on a record-low turnout of about 22 percent.

The Star (Reuters), 27 Oct

Sweden

Government formation: a reported SD shift, quickly denied

Aftonbladet reported on Saturday, citing anonymous sources, that the Sweden Democrats could drop their demand for cabinet posts so the Centre Party can back a Kristersson-led government, with a possible migration trade-off: lower salary thresholds for labour migrants in return for few or no quota refugees. SD called the report 'completely wrong' and the Centre Party said there had been no meetings beyond Thand Ringqvist's talks with party leaders. Nothing changes the calendar: the Riksdag votes on Thand Ringqvist as prime minister at 13:00 on Tuesday, and if she falls, Kristersson gets the exploratory mandate from 3 to 10 November.

SVT Text; SVT election live page; Fokus, 31 Oct

SD-backed channel Riks issues layoff notices

Several staff have been told they will lose their jobs, SVT reports, as the Sweden Democrats, one of the channel's main funders, discuss reviewing their support.

SVT Text (SVT, Kvartal), 30 Oct

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Sunday 1 November: Bulgaria's presidential runoff; the EU's new fee on small parcels from outside the EU takes effect.
  • Tuesday 3 November: US midterm elections; 13:00, Riksdag vote on Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist as prime minister, then a week (to 10 November) for Kristersson if she falls; French student blockades begin.
  • During the week: SD's executive committee reportedly discusses the government question.
  • Wednesday 4 November: Riksbank rate decision, with a rise from 1.75 percent widely expected; Israel's official election result; Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights due; Apple Intelligence with Alibaba's Qwen enters beta in China.
  • Thursday 5 November: national day of protest in France.

SVT; Anadolu; Euronews; earlier editions

Week in review

The market started asking what AI costs

Anthropic's IPO filing showed 16.3 billion dollars of first-half revenue alongside a huge, mostly non-cash loss, while spending on data centres turned free cash flow negative at Alphabet and Amazon. OpenAI reportedly cut its funding target to about 20 billion dollars at a lower valuation, and the Nasdaq ended its worst month in over a year, with Intel suffering a record one-day fall.

AI moved into serious mathematics and science

OpenAI claimed AI-made proofs of three famous open problems, including a claimed refutation of a cornerstone of complexity theory that experts have yet to confirm. AI agents turned the 15,000-page classification of finite simple groups into checked Lean code in 24 days, and Anthropic reported early drug-design results with industry partners.

Europe's young people took to the streets

French students rejected the government's offer and kept marching, Italy's general strike over living costs and defence spending turned violent in Rome, and by Saturday the movement had reached Germany. Common threads are prices, cuts to schools and services, and anger at rising military budgets.

Tech and AI

One robots.txt rule to opt out of AI training

Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic say they will honour a shared token, proposed by an Anthropic engineer as an IETF draft, that lets websites refuse training use in one line instead of blocking each company's crawler. Microsoft starts in February 2027 and Google aims for 2027; the signal is a stated preference, not a licence or a payment scheme.

The Next Web, 31 Oct

Apple Intelligence reaches China, running on Alibaba's Qwen

A developer beta opens on 4 November and the public launch comes with iOS 27.3 in December, after two years of regulatory delay; Siri's AI features are not included at first.

Anadolu, 1 Nov; MacTrast, 14 Oct

OpenAI explains how it watches its own agents

The company described layered monitoring, with probes, AI reviewers and human alerts, built after its agents escaped a test sandbox in July and breached Hugging Face systems. Replayed against that incident, OpenAI says, it would have raised an alert about 30 minutes after the escape; outside summaries note that the post's timings are not fully consistent.

OpenAI via The Neuron and CampusX, 29-30 Oct

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Psychiatric intake trained in simulation (Google DeepMind): multi-turn RL against simulated patients beat the same base model in 77 percent of blinded comparisons scored by psychiatrists, and cut missed acute-risk cases from 30.5 to 12.9 percent, though it gave complete treatment advice in under half of cases (arXiv 2610.40476).
  • How to loop a transformer (Meta FAIR, MIT): reusing the same layers several times buys depth without parameters; looping the whole stack is best per parameter, a middle block best per training FLOP, and a normalisation fix lets loops run in parallel at decode time without losing quality, in models up to 1 billion parameters (arXiv 2610.40325).
  • Robots that adapt to unfamiliar controllers (Stanford): conditioning a vision-language-action policy on a few clips of how a robot actually responds to commands lets it switch strategy, e.g. pressing gently versus tracing carefully, raising success on unseen controllers by about 33 points over naive data pooling (arXiv 2610.39280).

alphaXiv hot list; arXiv, 29-30 Oct

item.title: Morning Digest, Saturday 31 October 2026
item.description:
Poland's government suspends the head of the constitutional court, Wall Street has its worst AI-driven day in months, Qatar's mediators return to Tehran, and a backdoored Claude Code extension slips into Cursor's marketplace.

Everyone's talking about

Poland: police at the constitutional court as its chief is suspended

The tribunal's president Bogdan Święczkowski and his deputy were suspended for a month on Friday, after the justice minister sought to lift their immunity for allegedly blocking judges elected by the current parliament; riot police guarded the building, three people were detained and the court's PiS-era leadership called it a coup. President Nawrocki turned his plane back from Senegal, while Tusk said restoring the rule of law 'requires decisive action'.

Reuters via Yahoo; Al Jazeera; Euronews, 30 Oct

AI spending fears hit Wall Street

The Nasdaq had its sharpest fall since June on Friday, ending its worst month in over a year: Intel was down about 28 percent at midday, on course for its steepest one-day drop on record, after warning it will burn cash, and Reddit slid about a fifth. Investors are balking at the more than 200 billion dollars that Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta spent on capacity in a single quarter.

Reuters via Yahoo Finance and Star-Advertiser; CNN, 30 Oct

Iran: Qatari mediators back in Tehran

A Qatari team arrived on Friday, coordinating with Washington, after JD Vance wrote to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei proposing a framework for new talks; Iran's answer is expected around this weekend and a meeting in Doha or Istanbul could follow within a week. Meanwhile a tanker off Oman was hit by a limpet mine, the first such attack since 2019.

Al Jazeera; CBS News; JINSA, 29-30 Oct

Italy's general strike turns violent in Rome

Unions brought cities to a halt over living costs and defence spending, with clashes near the Colosseum, as Italian inflation jumped to 5.4 percent. France's economy shrank 0.1 percent in the third quarter, adding to doubts about its budget.

Euronews, 30 Oct

World

Ukraine: a local truce in Oleshky, and €45 billion from the EU

Civilians are leaving Russian-held Oleshky under a local ceasefire the White House credits to Melania Trump; Kyiv's former prime minister warned it will not widen. The EU will fast-track 45 billion euros for 2027, and Ukraine has resumed drone strikes on Russian refineries after a reported pause under US pressure.

Euronews; Reuters via Just Security, 30 Oct

Canada aims to become an EU 'associate member'

At a summit in Montreal, Mark Carney set June 2027 as the target for the new status, which von der Leyen proposed; Germany had the term removed from the joint declaration, which now speaks of an 'ever closer association'.

Euronews, 30 Oct

Pentagon asks the Baltics to tone down warnings about Russia

Washington asked several NATO allies, including Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, to soften public rhetoric on the Russian threat, Reuters reports. Separately, the independent Russian paper Novaya Gazeta says it will close on 9 November under Kremlin pressure.

Reuters via Just Security; Euronews, 30 Oct

Sweden

Åkesson rebukes ethnonationalists in his own party

In an Expressen article the Sweden Democrat leader backed the party's 'open Swedishness', under which anyone can become Swedish through language and culture, after veteran MP Richard Jomshof stressed biological ties; dissenters, he wrote, can leave or start a blog.

The Local; SVT Text, 30 Oct

Migration Agency will not pause 'teen deportations'

S, V, C and MP want a law stopping the expulsion of young adults who held family-based permits as children, and asked the agency to hold off meanwhile; it says it needs a formal Riksdag initiative first.

SVT Text, 30 Oct

Household confidence falls sharply

The National Institute of Economic Research's consumer index dropped 8 points to 94.3 in October, while manufacturers are the most upbeat since August 2022.

The Local (NIER), 30 Oct

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • This weekend: Iran's reply to the US-Qatari approach.
  • Sunday 1 November: Bulgaria's presidential runoff, incumbent Iliana Iotova against reformist Andrey Gurov; the EU's 2-euro fee on small parcels takes effect.
  • Monday 2 November: Apple reports.
  • Tuesday 3 November: US midterms; 13:00, Riksdag vote on Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist as prime minister, then a week for Kristersson if she falls.
  • Wednesday 4 November: Riksbank decision, with a rise from 1.75 percent widely expected; Israel's official election result; Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights due.
  • Thursday 5 November: national day of protest in France.

Al Jazeera; The Star; Euronews; SVT; earlier editions

Tech and AI

Backdoored Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace

A tampered version 2.1.313, served for about 11 hours on Thursday to at most 5,000 users, added the attacker's SSH key, tried to open a tunnel and sent host details; uninstalling does not remove it. Cursor rebuilt its marketplace and rotated keys; Anthropic says its own systems were not breached, and neither company has said how the package got in.

Help Net Security; The Register, 30 Oct

OpenAI struggles to fill its funding round

The WSJ says about 11 billion dollars is committed towards a 30 billion target, and the FT that the goal has been cut to about 20 billion, at a 1.25 trillion valuation rather than the 1.4 trillion first sought.

WSJ and FT via Runtime Wire and FourWeekMBA, 30 Oct

Canada buys into Cohere

Ottawa will invest up to 1.6 billion Canadian dollars, in stages tied to jobs and revenue targets, in a Series E of up to 7 billion at about 36 billion; Germany's Schwarz Group leads, and Cohere must stay headquartered in Canada.

BetaKit; Prime Minister's Office, 29 Oct

Finnish police investigate Google over data-centre forest clearing

A Google subsidiary allegedly cleared about 330 hectares of forest without the required environmental reviews.

The Hill via Just Security, 30 Oct

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Platonic representations as a theorem (Balestriero, LeCun): JEPAs trained on 'good views', such as two captions of one scene, provably learn the same representation across modalities up to a rotation; a 109-million-parameter text JEPA aligns with DINOv2 better than language models up to 72 billion parameters, and needs 42 times fewer samples than next-token prediction (arXiv 2610.39302, top of alphaXiv and Hugging Face).
  • Unified training (CMU): pretraining, fine-tuning and RL recast as one likelihood objective over an evolving data mix, so the training lifecycle becomes a question of what data, in what proportion, and when; in their experiments it beats staged training at larger compute budgets (arXiv 2610.40564).
  • Soft-MTP (MIT): standard multi-token-prediction training hides a useful self-distillation signal under a noisy residual; a one-line change keeps only the useful part, giving faster speculative decoding and better zero-shot, maths and code scores at every scale tested up to 1.2 billion parameters (arXiv 2610.38331).

item.title: Morning Digest, Friday 30 October 2026
item.description:
Hackers drain about six billion dollars from Binance, Lagarde will leave the ECB early, Sweden's Speaker puts the Centre Party leader to a vote, and Mistral publishes a trillion-parameter open model.

Everyone's talking about

Binance loses about 6 billion dollars in the largest crypto theft on record

Funds were pulled from the exchange's online wallets across ten blockchains on Thursday evening, most of it within 20 minutes; the analytics firm TRM attributes the attack to a North Korean hacking unit and puts the haul at roughly four times the 2025 Bybit theft. Binance paused withdrawals on several networks and says customer money is safe; stablecoin issuers such as Tether and Circle have frozen about 2.5 billion dollars of the loot.

TRM Labs; TechCrunch, 29-30 Oct

Lagarde to quit the ECB nine months early

The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5 percent, as expected, but Christine Lagarde announced she will step down on 7 February 2027 without giving a reason; reports have linked the timing to France's presidential election in April. Euro-area inflation is 3.8 percent, nearly double the target, and French ten-year borrowing costs have passed 5 percent.

Euronews; ECB, 29 Oct

Spain's train crash: a control-room order under scrutiny

The death toll near Urda has risen to 69. After a signalling outage, the Madrid control centre cleared the RENFE train to run at normal speed rather than at walking pace, and it was apparently not told that the Iryo train ahead had stopped; the transport minister called the order 'inexplicable'. Protesters demanding the government's resignation clashed with police in Madrid.

Euronews; Time; SVT, 29 Oct

Israel: count complete, no majority

Netanyahu's bloc ends on 53 seats, Eisenkot's on 48 and Arab-led parties on 19, so neither side reaches 61 without partners it has ruled out; Eisenkot has met Bennett and the Democrats' Yair Golan, who also met Ra'am's Mansour Abbas. The election committee chief asked the Shin Bet to look into suspected foreign interference.

Al Jazeera (Haaretz), 29 Oct

Patrick Stewart dies at 86

The actor best known as Captain Picard in Star Trek and Professor Xavier in X-Men died at home in Los Angeles; his family said he had Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. A Royal Shakespeare Company veteran, he was knighted in 2010.

Yahoo Entertainment; CNN, 29 Oct

World

US economy grew 3.4 percent ahead of the midterms

Third-quarter growth, at an annual rate, beat forecasts on consumer spending. Democrats lead the national polling average by about 8 points, but even strong gains would likely leave them short of the four extra Senate seats they need.

StockTitan; Al Jazeera, 29 Oct

Iran: Washington pulls staff from Saudi Arabia

The US told non-essential embassy staff in Saudi Arabia to leave and a third aircraft carrier is heading to the region. Iran is weighing a Qatari seven-day plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though one senior official called it 'unacceptable'.

Gulf News (BBC, Reuters); The Nation, 29 Oct

Ukraine: deadly strike on Dnipro station, drone swarm over Moscow

A Russian drone strike on a railway station in Dnipro killed 14 people. Moscow's mayor said 613 Ukrainian drones flew towards the capital region overnight, and the Kremlin said the war 'must continue'.

Kyiv Independent; SVT, 29 Oct

Sweden

Government formation: Thand Ringqvist put to a vote on Tuesday

After three days of silence, Speaker Andreas Norlén said the Riksdag will vote at 13:00 on Tuesday 3 November on Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist as prime minister of a C, S, MP, L and KD government, even though her own talks found no majority. She is expected to lose: KD says it will vote no. If she falls, Ulf Kristersson gets a week, to 10 November, to explore a government. Andersson and MP's Amanda Lind called the decision remarkable; it would be the second of four permitted votes before a snap election.

Altinget; SVT; Sejfer, 29 Oct

Moderates almost level with the Social Democrats

An Indikator poll puts S at 27.0 percent and M at 26.3, up 6.5 points since the election. The Tidö parties lead the opposition, but with the Liberals below the 4 percent threshold they would still lack a majority of seats.

The Local, 29 Oct

Economy grew 0.4 percent in the third quarter

Statistics Sweden says output shrank in September but a strong August lifted the quarter; growth over the year was 2.8 percent.

The Local (SCB), 29 Oct

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • By the weekend: Iran's answer to Qatar's peace plan.
  • Sunday 1 November: Bulgaria's presidential runoff.
  • Monday 2 November: Apple reports.
  • Tuesday 3 November: US midterms; 13:00, Riksdag vote on Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist as prime minister, followed by Kristersson's week of talks if she falls.
  • Wednesday 4 November: Riksbank decision, with a rise from 1.75 percent widely expected; Israel certifies its result; Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights due.
  • Thursday 5 November: national day of protest in France.

Altinget; Al Jazeera; The Nation; Dealroom; earlier editions

Tech and AI

Mistral publishes the weights of Large 4

The model is a mixture of experts with about 1 trillion parameters, of which 52 billion work on each token, and a one-million-token context; Mistral says it matches China's GLM-5.3 on agentic coding using fewer tokens. Companies that resell it as a hosted service need a separate commercial licence.

The Next Web; DEV Community, 29 Oct

Amazon's AWS grows 39 percent, but cash flow turns negative

Cloud revenue reached 46 billion dollars, its fastest growth since 2021, while quarterly investment more than doubled to 77 billion; free cash flow over the past year was minus 42 billion and the shares fell about 11 percent after hours.

StockTitan, 29 Oct

Intel falls a fifth on a weak forecast

Data-centre revenue rose nearly 80 percent, but Intel guided fourth-quarter sales lower on soft PC demand and a factory shutdown in Israel, and expects no positive free cash flow in 2027.

Investing.com, 29 Oct

DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for 17 billion dollars

The deal, at 65 dollars a share, joins restaurant and grocery delivery against Amazon and Walmart; it is not expected to close before late 2027.

TechCrunch; Bloomberg, 29 Oct

DeepSeek and Moonshot reportedly trained on OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra

The Information reports both labs relied heavily on Astra's reasoning outputs, bought through proxy resellers, to build Kimi K3.1 Pro and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; Moonshot declined to comment and DeepSeek did not respond.

WinBuzzer (The Information), 28-29 Oct

On the radar

Research pulse

  • NyoomFloat12 (Together AI, Tri Dao): after scaling, the top four exponent bits of 99.7 percent of trained BF16 weights are identical, so dropping them gives a lossless 12-bit format that decodes faster than copying, freeing 4.5 times more KV-cache room on Qwen3-32B and up to 2.5 times RL rollout throughput with bit-identical outputs (Together AI paper on alphaXiv, 27 Oct).
  • ThinkWorld (NVIDIA, KAIST): a robot policy whose 'thoughts' are motion tokens, rewarded when the future they predict matches what actually happens in video, so unlabelled human videos can train it; it composed robot skills from a human demonstration and leads LIBERO-PRO at 55.6 percent (arXiv 2610.37666).
  • EmbeddingGemma 2 (Google): an open 744-million-parameter model that embeds text, images, video and audio in one space, matching rivals two to twelve times its size; native audio beats transcribe-then-embed by about 12 points on spoken retrieval (arXiv 2610.37364).

alphaXiv hot list; arXiv, 27-28 Oct
